GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2014-07-21T10:36:07Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: events selector by name or complex id names
Description: I have an input with this complex name:

``` html
<input ... name="bic_voucher_entitybundle_company[name]" id="bic_voucher_entitybundle_company[name]" >
```

The problem comes when I want to assign this name or id to an event:

``` js
        events: {
            'click #bic_voucher_entitybundle_company[name]': 'limitLength',
            'click [name="bic_voucher_entitybundle_company[name]"]': 'limitLength',
```

Both do not work.


You must provide a category number (1-3). Your response must follow this format exactly:

CATEGORY: [category number]
REASONING: [your reasoning here, including specific reasons why an issue would be hard to dockerize if choosing category 3]
llm_response:
CATEGORY: 1
REASONING: This issue is about JavaScript event selectors not working with complex ID or name attributes containing square brackets. This is a conceptual issue related to CSS selector syntax in JavaScript, not a build environment problem. The issue can be analyzed and verified without needing to build or run any code. The problem is that square brackets have special meaning in CSS selectors (they're used for attribute selectors), so they need to be escaped when used in element IDs or names. The solution would involve proper escaping of these characters in the selector, which can be verified through code analysis without needing to set up a build environment. This is purely a syntax/knowledge issue that can be resolved by understanding how CSS selectors work with special characters.
